article.substack_body_markdown:
*Retrospective analysis, written on 1 November 2026 (GMT+7).* [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

An unchanged rate can still contain a pointed disagreement. On October 28, 2026, the Federal Reserve's policy committee voted 10-2 to keep the federal funds target range at 3.75 to 4 percent, according to its [[CITE:SOURCE_1|October 28 statement]]. Both dissenters wanted a quarter-percentage-point increase. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Capital Chronicle's reading is that the decision and its implementation answer different questions. The vote establishes the target range and the direction of disagreement. The companion note sets out the rates and instructions used to implement that stance. A reader needs both documents to distinguish the policy choice from its operating settings. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]] [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

## A hold with dissent in one direction

Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack voted against the action because they preferred to raise the target range by a quarter percentage point at that meeting. That makes the direction of dissent clear: they favored an increase, while the approved action maintained the range. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

The statement described economic activity as expanding strongly, domestic spending as resilient and inflation as elevated. It also said accumulating more information would help the Committee determine the stance appropriate for a timely return to its 2 percent inflation goal. That is the Committee's published assessment; it should not be turned into a separate explanation attributed to either dissenter. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

The strongest countercase to a looming-hike interpretation is the decision itself: ten members approved keeping the range unchanged. The two dissenters' preference is evidence of disagreement at this meeting, not a forecast of the next vote. Reading the split as a timetable for higher rates would give it a meaning the vote alone cannot establish. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

## One target range, several operating rates

The [[CITE:SOURCE_2|companion implementation note]] describes decisions to carry out the October 28 policy stance. The Board of Governors unanimously maintained interest paid on reserve balances at 3.90 percent, effective October 29. The directive to the New York Fed's trading desk, also effective October 29, instructed it to undertake operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate within the 3.75 to 4 percent target range. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

The same directive set standing overnight repo operations at 4.0 percent and the standing overnight reverse repo offering rate at 3.75 percent. In a related action, the Board unanimously approved the primary credit rate at its existing 4.0 percent level. The note therefore assigns some identical numbers to different instruments; it does not combine those instruments into a single rate. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

The 3.90 percent reserve-balances setting is not a substitute label for the 3.75 to 4 percent federal funds target range. One is an individual rate; the other is the interval the desk is instructed to maintain. Likewise, unanimous Board actions on reserve interest and primary credit should not be mistaken for unanimity in the 10-2 FOMC decision. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]] [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

These are announced settings, not observations of the rates at which market transactions actually took place. The chart compares their stated levels and roles. It should not be read as a record of market repricing or as a measure of how effectively the instruments transmitted the decision. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

## What to watch in a later decision

The next useful question is whether a later Committee decision changes the target range or the direction of the recorded vote. The October 28 documents should be read as that meeting's decision and implementation instructions, rather than a prediction of what comes next. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]] [[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

*Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.* [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

visual_editorial_decision.channel_media_limits: Private preview choices only. Each selected figure must retain legible metric, units, period, source and announcement/observation distinction at the destination's displayed size. Do not crop away the dissent direction, effective-date qualification or announced-settings label. No upload, platform draft or send is authorized.

data_spec.chart_form: Two horizontal bars with a shared zero-based axis labelled Members. Directly label counts and action preferences. Use restrained distinguishable colors and text labels; show the named dissenters in a readable annotation. No pie, gauge, implied probability scale or pictorial heads.
data_spec.missingness: Individual majority names and individual rationales are not supplied. Do not infer them.

observations.decision: Maintain the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent

data_spec.source_credit: Source: Federal Reserve Board, October 28, 2026 FOMC statement.
data_spec.source_series: October 28, 2026 FOMC statement vote on the announced monetary-policy action; single-meeting categorical counts, not a time series
data_spec.transform: Code extracts the literal counts and maps the exact 1/4-percentage-point preference to the decimal 0.25 using exact decimal arithmetic. No vote percentages, probability conversion, extrapolation or forecast; do not construct a hypothetical resulting target range.
data_spec.unit: members for vote counts; percentage points for the quoted dissent preference
data_spec.value_status: actual announced vote and explicitly recorded dissent preference

charts.placement_after: A hold with dissent in one direction
charts.question: What did the majority approve, and in which direction did the dissenters disagree?
charts.why_useful: A two-category vote comparison joins the strength of the majority to the direction of dissent. It prevents an undifferentiated split-vote graphic from suggesting the dissenters wanted a cut or that the committee was evenly divided. Name the two dissenters beside their preference; do not invent a majority-member roster.

data_spec.chart_form: Horizontal interval-and-dot plot with a separately labelled target-range row and one row per operating setting. Shared percent axis, direct endpoint and point labels; distinguish the band from dots and each instrument by its full label. A clearly labelled local axis is acceptable for point positions; do not use truncated bars or imply rate changes through line connections. State Announced settings, not observed market rates within the figure.
data_spec.context_boundary: SOURCE_2 remains the retained official companion-note context. Attribute its settings to that note within the historical cutoff; do not upgrade it to an independent second confirmation of the FOMC vote or any market outcome.
data_spec.missingness: No effective federal funds rate, utilization, transaction rates, prior-meeting values or transmission outcomes are admitted. Leave all absent. Do not label facilities as hard market floors or ceilings.

observations.series: Standing overnight reverse repo offering rate

observations.timing_note: Existing level in related Board action; do not invent a distinct new effective date

data_spec.period: Announced October 28, 2026; implementation directive and reserve-balances setting effective October 29, 2026. Primary credit described as existing in the related Board action.
data_spec.private_scope: Use within this private retained-source operation only. The feed's public_republication_authority=false is preserved; this decision creates no public release authority.
data_spec.source_credit: Source: Federal Reserve Board, October 28, 2026 FOMC statement and implementation note.
data_spec.source_series: Single announcement's target-range endpoints and instrument-specific implementation settings; an announced cross-section, not realized interest-rate observations
data_spec.transform: Code maps the literal fractional target endpoint to decimal percent and normalizes display precision to two decimal places. Plot exact announced values. No interpolation, averaging, midpoint, inferred spread, yield-curve construction or historical comparison.
data_spec.value_status: actual announced policy settings; effective date remains distinct from announcement and historical observation

charts.placement_after: One target range, several operating rates
charts.question: Which announced rates define the target band, and which are settings for separate operating instruments?
charts.why_useful: A shared-rate-axis comparison makes the target interval visually distinct from the individual administered settings. It prevents the 3.90 percent reserve-balances rate from being mistaken for the federal funds target or an observed market rate, and it shows that equal numeric settings can belong to different instruments.

visual_editorial_decision.classification_rationale: This is a substantive but bounded document-led explanation, so retain ANALYSIS and two useful charts. A historical time series is unnecessary for these categorical and cross-sectional questions. Do not convert it into a NEWS/POLICY exception merely to reduce media requirements. Two charts answer different reader questions; no third chart is justified by the packet.
visual_editorial_decision.countercase: The majority approved the hold. Two dissenters favoring an increase do not establish an imminent hike, a tightening probability, or the views of the ten supporters beyond this decision. Several implementation settings, including unanimous Board actions, do not make the FOMC vote unanimous or establish a separate change in the policy stance. The retained documents do not explain each member's reasoning.
visual_editorial_decision.editorial_thesis: Explain two separate dimensions of the retained October 28 documents: the 10-2 decision maintained the federal funds target range while the named dissenters preferred a quarter-percentage-point increase; the companion implementation note specified different settings for distinct instruments. The vote describes the decision and disagreement, while the operating settings describe implementation. Neither document establishes a future rate path, a policy surprise, or a market reaction.

material_claim_bindings.support_excerpt:
The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.

Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release PDF October 28, 2026 Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT Share The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote:

The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability. Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 3.90 percent, effective October 29, 2026.

Home News & Events Press Releases Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement Press Release October 28, 2026 Implementation Note issued October 28, 2026 Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on October 28, 2026:

As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective October 29, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 4.0 percent. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.75 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. When appropriate, increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury bills and, if needed, other Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less to maintain an ample level of reserves. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 4.0 percent.

Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 4.0 percent.
